title: Michigan: history overview
d: Michigan: the Great Lakes State, admitted 1837 (26th); capital Lansing.
definition: Michigan: the Great Lakes State, admitted 1837 (26th); capital Lansing.
description: Michigan — "Great Lakes State" — entered the Union 1837 (26th). Its capital is Lansing and its largest city is Detroit. Ojibwe; French then British. This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Michigan achieved statehood 1837 (26th). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Auto industry; Detroit boom. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Michigan its number among the states.

title: The statehood story
d: How Michigan went from territory to state.
definition: How Michigan went from territory to state.
description: The statehood story of Michigan: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. Deindustrialization; comeback. Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Michigan's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Lansing
d: Lansing is the capital of Michigan.
definition: Lansing is the capital of Michigan.
description: Lansing has been the seat of Michigan government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Michigan's largest is Detroit — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Great Lakes State
d: Michigan is known as "Great Lakes State."
definition: Michigan is known as "Great Lakes State."
description: The nickname "Great Lakes State" captures how Michigan sees itself — and how America sees it. The auto industry made Detroit the Motor City. State nicknames come from history, geography, or industry, and they appear on license plates, tourism campaigns, and sports teams. The motto goes deeper: "Si quaeris peninsulam amoenam circumspice (If you seek a pleasant peninsula, look about you)."
